title: PKINIT followed by self-targeted U2U
description: Correlates certificate-associated Kerberos AS issuance with a self-targeted U2U request using the same ticket fingerprint. A timely response matching the original account and requested service raises a notice. Related flows must reach the same Zeek worker.

topics.title: Load Kerberos, Notice, and X.509 scripts
topics.description: @load imports Kerberos analysis, the Notice framework, and X.509 file analysis. These scripts supply protocol events, notice output, and certificate observations used by later handlers. Lines beginning ## are documentation comments. Related Kerberos flows must reach the same Zeek worker so their observations share the correlation tables.
links: Record Kerberos file observations before AS processing
Index worker-local tables and expire from creation

topics.title: Give the exported notice a namespace
topics.description: module PKINIT_U2U scopes subsequent identifiers to that namespace. Inside export, redef enum Notice::Type += adds Self_Targeted_Ticket to the framework's existing enumeration and exposes it to other scripts. The later NOTICE call uses this member to classify the finding and attach its connection and evidence.
links: Record emission and submit a typed framework notice

topics.title: Set correlation age, reply age, and origin capacity
topics.description: const declares values that &redef allows site policy to override. The interval literals 5min and 30sec set the origin correlation window and pending response window. max_ticket_states uses count and defaults to 100000 origin entries. The correlation window starts at successful AS issuance; the response window bounds request-to-response pairing.
links: Index worker-local tables and expire from creation
Require a ticket identity and available origin capacity

topics.title: Select the Zeek 9 wire-bit mapping
topics.description: T is Zeek's Boolean true. legacy_zeek9_kdc_bits defaults to T for the documented Zeek 9.0.0 mapping of wire 0x8 to renewable_ok. RFC 4120 assigns that bit to ENC-TKT-IN-SKEY. Setting F selects enc_tkt_in_skey for a parser with a verified corrected mapping.
links: Select the U2U flag through the compatibility branch

topics.title: Model AS request identity and qualification
topics.description: AS_Pending is a record with named fields. signature, client, and realm hold strings; qualified holds a bool and defaults to F. The request handler sets qualified from certificate and field-presence checks. Tracking both ordinary and qualifying requests gives the overlap checks a common record for each connection.
links: Retain AS timing, nonce, and ambiguity
Construct pending AS state with optional fallbacks

topics.title: Retain AS timing, nonce, and ambiguity
topics.description: started has type time and records the request observation timestamp. nonce has type count and retains the request's nonnegative nonce. ambiguous defaults to F and becomes T when a distinct request overlaps. AS response pairing uses pending connection state, overlap status, response age, certificate observations, and account identity.
links: Require timely, same-account, certificate-linked TGT issuance

topics.title: Store account and issuance context for a ticket
topics.description: Origin records a successful AS issuance: client and realm identify the account, issued stores its timestamp, uid stores the original connection identifier, and source stores an addr. The origins table indexes this record by ticket fingerprint, linking later requests to the retained ticket and its account context.
links: Retain the first successful issuance timestamp
Link issued, authenticating, and additional tickets by fingerprint

topics.title: Model the target and authenticating ticket
topics.description: TGS_Pending stores the request signature, authenticating TGT fingerprint, requested service, and realm. Each colon assigns a field's type. qualified defaults to F and changes to T after the request passes all candidate checks. Retaining the target separately lets the response handler compare the issued ticket's service and realm with the request.
links: Retain TGS timing, nonce, and ambiguity
Store TGS request state before candidate checks

topics.title: Retain TGS timing, nonce, and ambiguity
topics.description: started stores the absolute request time for response-age comparisons. nonce retains the request's count value, and ambiguous defaults to F. The closing }; completes TGS_Pending. Request qualification requires nonce presence; response association uses the pending connection record, overlap status, timing, and account and ticket comparisons.
links: Quarantine a distinct overlapping TGS request
Require fresh, qualified response state and emission eligibility

topics.title: Index worker-local tables and expire from creation
topics.description: table[string] of AS_Pending maps a connection UID to a pending AS record. origins maps a ticket fingerprint to Origin; auth_ticket maps a UID to a fingerprint; tgs_pending maps a UID to TGS_Pending. &create_expire bases retention on insertion. Explicit age checks enforce the logical windows. Each worker holds its own tables.
links: Set correlation age, reply age, and origin capacity
Retain the first successful issuance timestamp
Store TGS request state before candidate checks

topics.title: Track emission, certificate direction, and quarantine
topics.description: emitted stores ticket-fingerprint membership. pkinit_cert uses set[string, bool] to distinguish originator and responder certificate observations for each UID. Their &create_expire attributes set retention from insertion. quarantined retains ambiguous UIDs until connection removal. Later handlers use add to insert membership, in to test it, and delete to remove it.
links: Record Kerberos file observations before AS processing
Release quarantine when connection state is removed

topics.title: Record Kerberos file observations before AS processing
topics.description: file_over_new_connection receives typed fa_file, connection, and bool arguments. The || condition accepts f$source values "KRB" or "KRB_TCP". add pkinit_cert[c$uid, is_orig] records the UID and direction as a compound key. The documented parser order delivers these certificate file observations before the enclosing AS event.
links: Consume the request-side certificate observation once
Consume the responder certificate and require pending state

topics.title: Check ciphertext presence before fingerprinting
topics.description: ticket_id accepts a KRB::Ticket and returns a string. ?$ tests optional ciphertext presence before $ retrieves its value. Short-circuit || stops evaluation when the presence check fails. The function returns "" for absent or empty ciphertext, giving callers a sentinel they can check before storing a ticket identity.
links: Hash delimited ticket metadata and encrypted content
Require a ticket identity and available origin capacity

topics.title: Hash delimited ticket metadata and encrypted content
topics.description: cat joins the lowercased realm and service name, cipher number, and ciphertext with explicit NUL separators. fmt("%d", ticket$cipher) converts the number to text. sha256_hash returns a digest of that combined value. The digest serves as the continuity key linking an issued TGT, an authenticating ticket, and an additional ticket.
links: Select the AP-REQ embedded in KDC preauthentication
Require U2U and exactly one matching additional ticket
Link issued, authenticating, and additional tickets by fingerprint

topics.title: Require the realm and local krbtgt service together
topics.description: local_tgt returns bool. && requires both the ticket realm and service comparisons to succeed. to_lower makes them case-insensitive; cat("krbtgt/", realm) builds the expected local TGT service name. The AS response handler uses this predicate before retaining an origin for later ticket correlation.
links: Require timely, same-account, certificate-linked TGT issuance

topics.title: Select the U2U flag through the compatibility branch
topics.description: The ternary condition ? true_value : false_value selects a Boolean field. With legacy_zeek9_kdc_bits=T, wire_u2u reads opts$renewable_ok; F selects opts$enc_tkt_in_skey. The request handler first checks kdc_options presence, then combines this flag with ticket continuity, additional-ticket count, request identity, and self-target checks.
links: Require U2U and exactly one matching additional ticket

topics.title: Consume the request-side certificate observation once
topics.description: krb_as_request receives a connection and KRB::KDC_Request. [c$uid, T] in pkinit_cert retrieves originator-side certificate membership, and delete consumes it for this request. A quarantined UID returns immediately. Otherwise sha256_hash combines the certificate status and formatted message into a signature used to detect distinct overlapping AS requests.
links: Construct pending AS state with optional fallbacks

topics.title: Quarantine distinct outstanding AS requests
topics.description: in tests whether the UID already has a pending AS record. A different signature, detected with !=, sets that record's $ambiguous field to T and adds the UID to quarantined. The outer branch returns for both duplicates and distinct overlaps, preserving the original pending record and its timestamp. Quarantine lasts until connection removal.
links: Track emission, certificate direction, and quarantine
Construct pending AS state with optional fallbacks
Release quarantine when connection state is removed

topics.title: Construct pending AS state with optional fallbacks
topics.description: AS_Pending($field=value, ...) constructs a typed record. ?$ tests each optional field before a ternary chooses its value or an empty-string or zero fallback. network_time() records the observation time. qualified requires a certificate signal and client name, service realm, and nonce presence. as_pending[c$uid] stores the record for this connection.
links: Model AS request identity and qualification
Consume the responder certificate and require pending state

topics.title: Consume the responder certificate and require pending state
topics.description: krb_as_response reads [c$uid, F] membership and immediately deletes that responder-side certificate observation. The || guard returns when the UID is quarantined or !in as_pending. Processing continues for a pending request on an eligible connection, carrying the consumed certificate status into the subsequent AS response checks.
links: Consume pending AS state before checking the reply
Require timely, same-account, certificate-linked TGT issuance

topics.title: Consume pending AS state before checking the reply

ranges.code:
local a = as_pending[c$uid];
delete as_pending[c$uid];

topics.description: local a retrieves the pending AS record after the membership guard. delete as_pending[c$uid] then consumes the association before response validation. Each accepted pending request supplies one response-processing attempt. A later response needs fresh request state to reach the same checks.
links: Require timely, same-account, certificate-linked TGT issuance

topics.title: Require timely, same-account, certificate-linked TGT issuance

ranges.code:
if ( a$qualified == F || a$ambiguous || network_time()-a$started > response_window ||
certificate_seen == F || ! msg?$client_realm ||
to_lower(a$client) != to_lower(msg$client_name) ||
to_lower(a$realm) != to_lower(msg$client_realm) ||
! local_tgt(msg$ticket, msg$client_realm) )
return;

topics.description: The || chain returns on any failed prerequisite. Continuing requires a qualified, unambiguous AS request, response age at most response_window, a responder certificate observation, a present client_realm, matching account and realm, and a local-realm TGT. to_lower makes identity comparisons case-insensitive, and the optional realm check precedes its value access.
links: Require the realm and local krbtgt service together
Require a ticket identity and available origin capacity

topics.title: Require a ticket identity and available origin capacity
topics.description: ticket_id computes the ticket continuity key. Processing continues when the key is nonempty and |origins| is below max_ticket_states. Vertical bars count table entries; >= triggers the capacity return. This origin-table admission check occurs before the later key-membership test, including when the observed key already has an origin record.
links: Set correlation age, reply age, and origin capacity
Retain the first successful issuance timestamp

topics.title: Retain the first successful issuance timestamp
topics.description: key !in origins admits the first retained observation for a ticket fingerprint. Origin copies account, realm, UID, and originator address from the successful exchange. $issued=network_time() starts the correlation window. Repeated observations of a retained key preserve that timestamp; later requests use the same fingerprint to retrieve this origin.
links: Store account and issuance context for a ticket
Select the AP-REQ embedded in KDC preauthentication

topics.title: Select the AP-REQ embedded in KDC preauthentication
topics.description: krb_ap_request receives a Ticket, AP_Options, and an in_kdc_padata bool. The handler continues when in_kdc_padata is T, selecting an AP-REQ embedded in KDC preauthentication. ticket_id computes that authenticating ticket's fingerprint for the enclosing TGS request. The event signature explicitly carries the context needed to select this path.
links: Cache the authenticating key for the enclosing request
Require U2U and exactly one matching additional ticket

topics.title: Cache the authenticating key for the enclosing request
topics.description: The documented parser order emits this AP event before the enclosing TGS request. A different existing auth_ticket value causes the handler to store ""; the else branch stores the observed key. Each invocation follows this comparison anew. The UID-keyed string entry expires under response_window and is consumed by the TGS request handler.
links: Consume the authenticating ticket and fingerprint the request
Index worker-local tables and expire from creation

topics.title: Consume the authenticating ticket and fingerprint the request
topics.description: A membership test and ternary retrieve auth_ticket[c$uid], using "" as the fallback. delete consumes the cached value before the quarantine guard. For an eligible UID, sha256_hash combines the key and formatted request into an overlap signature. Later code records ordinary requests as well as candidates, then applies qualification checks.
links: Quarantine a distinct overlapping TGS request
Store TGS request state before candidate checks

topics.title: Quarantine a distinct overlapping TGS request
topics.description: An existing tgs_pending entry triggers overlap handling. If its signature differs, the handler sets $ambiguous=T and adds the UID to quarantined. Ordinary and candidate requests both participate. The branch returns for either a duplicate or distinct overlap, preserving the existing pending request for the response guard and eventual cleanup.
links: Track emission, certificate direction, and quarantine
Store TGS request state before candidate checks
Release quarantine when connection state is removed

topics.title: Store TGS request state before candidate checks

ranges.code:
# Track ordinary requests too. Otherwise an earlier ordinary reply could be
# mistaken for a later candidate on a pipelined connection.
tgs_pending[c$uid] = TGS_Pending($signature=signature, $tgt=key,
$service=msg?$service_name ? msg$service_name : "",
$realm=msg?$service_realm ? msg$service_realm : "",
$started=network_time(), $nonce=msg?$nonce ? msg$nonce : 0);

topics.description: The table assignment constructs TGS_Pending with its signature, authenticating key, requested service and realm, start time, and nonce. ?$ checks and ternary fallbacks supply empty strings or zero for absent optional fields. qualified keeps its F default at this point. Recording every request lets overlap handling account for ordinary requests interleaved with candidates.
links: Model the target and authenticating ticket
Require U2U and exactly one matching additional ticket

topics.title: Require U2U and exactly one matching additional ticket

ranges.code:
if ( key == "" || key !in origins ||
! msg?$kdc_options || ! wire_u2u(msg$kdc_options) ||
! msg?$additional_tickets || |msg$additional_tickets| != 1 ||
! msg?$service_name || ! msg?$service_realm || ! msg?$nonce ||
ticket_id(msg$additional_tickets[0]) != key )
return;

topics.description: The || chain allows processing to continue with a retained origin key, present kdc_options, a true wire U2U flag, exactly one additional ticket, and present service name, realm, and nonce. |msg$additional_tickets| checks vector length before [0] access. ticket_id(msg$additional_tickets[0]) must equal the authenticating key, linking both observed tickets.

topics.title: Bound origin age and require the original account as target
topics.description: origins[key] retrieves the retained AS origin after membership has been checked. The request time must be at or after issuance and within correlation_window. to_lower comparisons require the requested service realm and service name to equal the origin's realm and client account. Passing these checks reaches the candidate qualification assignment.

Mark the request after all candidate checks pass

topics.title: Mark the request after all candidate checks pass

ranges.code:
tgs_pending[c$uid]$qualified = T;
}

topics.description: tgs_pending[c$uid]$qualified = T updates one field of the existing pending request. Reaching this assignment means the ticket, flag, identity, and origin-age guards passed. The response handler later consumes this marker and requires a timely matching response before recording emission and creating the notice.
links: Require and consume the pending TGS association
Require fresh, qualified response state and emission eligibility

topics.title: Require and consume the pending TGS association
topics.description: krb_tgs_response continues for an eligible UID with a pending TGS request; quarantined or missing-state UIDs return. local t retrieves the record, then delete tgs_pending[c$uid] consumes the association before further checks. Each pending entry supplies one response-processing attempt, following the same consumption pattern as AS responses.
links: Require fresh, qualified response state and emission eligibility

topics.title: Require fresh, qualified response state and emission eligibility

ranges.code:
if ( t$qualified == F || t$ambiguous || t$tgt !in origins || t$tgt in emitted ||
network_time() < t$started || network_time()-t$started > response_window ||
! msg?$client_realm )
return;

topics.description: The || guard allows a qualified, unambiguous request with a retained origin and a ticket fingerprint eligible for its first emission. The response time must be at or after the request, its age at most response_window, and client_realm present. The emitted set tracks script-level duplicate status; the Notice framework applies additional output suppression.

topics.title: Match the response account and issued service ticket

ranges.code:
local o = origins[t$tgt];
if ( network_time()-o$issued > correlation_window ||
to_lower(msg$client_name) != to_lower(o$client) ||
to_lower(msg$client_realm) != to_lower(o$realm) ||
to_lower(msg$ticket$realm) != to_lower(t$realm) ||
to_lower(msg$ticket$service_name) != to_lower(t$service) )
return;

topics.description: origins[t$tgt] retrieves the retained AS account. The response must fall within correlation_window, name that account and realm, and carry a ticket whose realm and service match the pending target. Chained $ access reads fields inside the ticket. Passing every comparison reaches the linked self-targeted U2U issuance notice.
links: Record emission and submit a typed framework notice

topics.title: Record emission and submit a typed framework notice
topics.description: add emitted[t$tgt] records the ticket fingerprint before NOTICE is called. The bracketed record supplies $note=Self_Targeted_Ticket, $conn=c, the fingerprint identifier, and correlation_window as the suppression interval. $field=value initializes notice fields. The emitted set guards repeated findings during its retention; the framework also applies identifier-based suppression.
links: Format the account and realm in notice output
Match the response account and issued service ticket

topics.title: Format the account and realm in notice output
topics.description: fmt fills %s placeholders with client name and realm from the accepted response. $msg reports linked self-targeted U2U ticket issuance, and $sub formats account@realm. The terminating ]); closes the notice record and call. Placeholder mappings bind these displayed values to the exact source expressions supplying them.

topics.title: Clear AS pending state on Kerberos errors
topics.description: krb_error receives an observed KRB::Error_Msg. delete as_pending[c$uid] discards the pending AS association for that connection. A later AS response needs fresh request state to proceed. Retained successful origins and emitted fingerprints follow their own expiration lifetimes, keeping established ticket context separate from the failed exchange's pending state.
links: Clear request context and retain quarantine
Consume the responder certificate and require pending state

topics.title: Clear request context and retain quarantine

ranges.before:
# Advertised preauth methods in KRB-ERROR never establish PKINIT success.
delete as_pending[c$uid];

topics.description: The delete statements clear the UID's authenticating-ticket cache, pending TGS record, and both direction-specific certificate observations. Deleting an absent entry is harmless, so this cleanup covers partially observed exchanges. Quarantine persists across Kerberos errors and timer expiration; connection_state_remove is the handler that releases the UID's quarantine membership.
links: Release quarantine when connection state is removed
Track emission, certificate direction, and quarantine

topics.title: Release quarantine when connection state is removed
topics.description: connection_state_remove runs when Zeek discards the connection state. The handler deletes the UID from quarantined and clears pending AS, authenticating-ticket, and pending TGS entries. Ticket-keyed origins retain their independent correlation-window expiration, allowing a later connection on the same worker to reference a still-retained ticket.
links: Remove both directions of certificate context
Index worker-local tables and expire from creation

topics.title: Remove both directions of certificate context
topics.description: The final delete statements remove [c$uid, T] and [c$uid, F], covering originator and responder certificate observations when the connection ends. Each key contains both the UID string and direction bool. Connection cleanup removes any remaining observations, complementing the pkinit_cert set's response-window expiration.

ranges.code:

! msg?$kdc_options || ! wire_u2u(msg$kdc_options) ||
! msg?$additional_tickets || |msg$additional_tickets| != 1 ||
! msg?$service_name || ! msg?$service_realm || ! msg?$nonce ||

topics.description: The fingerprint helper hashes ticket metadata and ciphertext. The AP-REQ supplies the authenticating key, and the TGS request requires its single additional ticket to produce the same key. The retained AS origin links that key to successful certificate-associated issuance. The TGS response then confirms the original account and requested self-targeted service.
